newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power mixed in thin holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power mixed in thin holiday trade.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mixed Friday in extremely thin trade, as a rising thermometer dissuaded some buyers from entering the market.
"I think everyone is in pretty good shape. A lot of people got most stuff done before the holidays," one market source said, noting many traders were absent today.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery were discussed in the $16.00-$17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, as compared with Thursday's $17.50-19.00 trading range.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power for Monday was pegged at $10.00-$11.50, off from Thursday's levels around $12.00.
Separately, a 420 megawatt (MW) Big Stone coal-fired generating plant in South Dakota was shut Thursday for repairs and was expected to stay off line at least for a couple of days.
The 538 MW Duane Arnold nuclear station in Palo, Iowa, was operating at 68 percent early Friday after a recirculation pump tripped on Thursday.
Temperatures in the MAPP region are expected to moderate this weekend, but a cold blast of air will likely arrive early next week, dragging temperatures in the northern part below normal.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday were still valued at $17.50-$20.00 in very light trade. Bids were heard in the $15.00-17.00 area.
MAIN off peak power for Monday was assessed around $12.00.
Temperatures in the MAIN region are expected to moderate through Sunday to much above-normal but then dip back to seasonable levels by Tuesday.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday were notionally in the $12.00-14.00 range, as compared with Thursday's $11.50-12.50 trading range.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery was quoted again at $11.00-$13.00.
Temperatures in the ECAR region are forecast to climb to above-normal levels this weekend and into Monday.
Separately, Consumers Power Co's 780 MW Palisades nuclear unit in South Haven, Mich., restarted early Friday.

Also, Detroit Edison's 1,116 MW Fermi 2 nuclear unit in Newport, Mich., is expected to restart today following a series of restart snags since its shutdown for maintenance and refueling on September 27.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), where temperatures are expected to climb to about 15-20 degrees above-normal this weekend and into early next week, peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery were in the $13.50-$14.50 range, down from Thursday's range of $15.00-$20.00.
These prices reflect much softer natural gas prices in Texas where deals were confirmed done around $3 per million British thermal units for the weekend.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for Monday delivery were assessed around $12.00, compared with $11.00-14.00 on Thursday.
January/February peak prices in SPP were down in the $22.00-23.00 range, as compared with the $23.50-$25.00 range seen on Thursday.
((--H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628))
